title: Total influence of linear thresholds
statement: For every natural number $n$, if $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ is a linear threshold function, then its total influence, the sum over coordinates $i$ of $\mathbb E[(f(x)-f(x^i))^2/4]$ under uniform $x$, is at most $\sqrt n$. Here $x^i$ is obtained by flipping coordinate $i$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a linear threshold function, represented by a polynomial threshold of degree at most one
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. Set $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]$ and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$, where $x^{\{i\}}$ flips bit $i$. If $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_+(c+\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i})$ for some real $c,a_i$, then $I(f)\le\sqrt n$.
